findings.text: follow-on: alone_counts globs runs*.txt, which matches both the cumulative runs.txt and each per-id runs-<id>.txt, so a row present in both is counted twice; the handoff id's five base rows appear in both files and the manifest therefore records base_fail 10 where its five base-alone logs report 5. The verdict is unaffected, but a recorded alone count that does not reconcile with the log it cites is a measurement a later reader cannot check.

follow-on: the file the manifest names as the aggregate alone-run index holds 15 of the 80 alone rows (compact progress's 10 plus the handoff id's 5 base rows), so a reader taking it for the complete index finds no runs recorded for the other seven ids and for handoff's candidate arm.

item_verdicts.diff: the node commits nothing, so it has no diff of its own; its reviewed revision pair is b3315147a4845df5755a6b769470d08057ed8806 at both ends, and the tree it measured carries both runs' changes, confirmed on reckon/crew/reports.py:1146, tests/conftest.py:1398 and reckon/flight.py:458.
item_verdicts.done_when: the fence requires lowercase rev= labels, host and literal command, module.__file__ under each checkout, the whole-suite summary line at each revision and EXIT=; whole-suite-arms/base-d133f043.log and candidate-131faa43.log carry every one of these, and the manifest records the 8 added ids with alone counts and a verdict each.
item_verdicts.goal: the goal is a whole-suite measurement at base d133f04391fa2e21fe142934fcd857dd9c0e7780 and at the stacked candidate 131faa43ddcc96a86f3ec625aeac9d93e2cb65dc of the revision-label and leak-scan runs; both arms ran, and candidate 131faa43's two parents (0620f793, a merge of base with d474ea8, and 837cee27) put both runs' changes in the tree it measured.
item_verdicts.manifest: read in full — it records the base arm at 31 failed/14192 passed and the candidate at 33 failed/14195 passed with log paths, derives 8 added ids, gives each alone counts and a verdict (four also at base, four load-only), and states no added id is attributable to either run's files.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the declared scope is the reports directory .../reports/reckon/the-suite-is-green-at-head/stacked-revision-label-and-leak-scan-whole-suite-at-merge with the repository read-only; manifest changed_paths is none and every artefact named lies under whole-suite-arms/ in the run directory or under that reports path.

justifications.durability: the node lands no code, so there is no regression surface for a test to guard, and its declared negative control (none: a measurement of an existing merge candidate adds no test of its own) is the correct form for the role.
justifications.evidence: the arm logs carry the required header and summary lines and the 8 added ids reproduce independently from them, but whole-suite-arms/finalize_manifest.py:80 records base_fail 10 for the handoff id where its five base-alone logs each report exactly one failure.
justifications.fit: the arm header lines in whole-suite-arms/base-d133f043.log:1 follow the shape the fence dictates (rev=, host=, cmd=, module.__file__) and no path or symbol the node wrote carries a plan or version identifier.
justifications.goal_fidelity: both arms exist at the revisions the goal names (whole-suite-arms/base-d133f043.log:1, whole-suite-arms/candidate-131faa43.log:1) and candidate 131faa43's ancestry carries both d474ea8 and 837cee27, so both runs are measured.
justifications.reuse: the added-id derivation delegates to the repository's own reckon.crew.review.added_failures_from_gate_logs (whole-suite-arms/derive_added.py:20) rather than re-implementing a gate-log reader, so the node extends that owner.
justifications.scope_discipline: the node changed no repository file (manifest changed_paths: none) and wrote its scripts, indexes and logs only under whole-suite-arms/ in its own run directory, with report.md under the declared reports path.
